description: Every relevant Dibbla operation with exactly one state. A capability belongs in /platform only when a stable API backs it, it needs no caller filesystem, keyring, TTY or external binary, and it either finishes promptly or returns a durable pollable ID.

states.summary: Exposed remotely, no side effects. Cannot acknowledge, refresh, rotate or mark-read as a hidden convenience.
Exposed remotely, mutates, uses an idempotency key.
Exposed remotely, requires an accurate destructiveHint, a bound read-only plan and a distinct human approval.
Exposed remotely, returns a durable operation ID that is polled. An MCP call never holds a long run open.
Deliberately never remote. Requires a stated reason.
Intended but not exposed. Requires an owning proposal or API dependency.

capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-534 (P-0035 Part B) on mcp-server's OAuth-protected /platform toolset; listed in tools/list only for a grant holding the scope, and refused server-side otherwise.

capabilities.title: Update an application's configuration
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-535 (P-0035 Part B) on mcp-server's OAuth-protected /platform toolset: the safe configuration update — non-secret environment variables by name (merge, never replace), replicas, cpu and memory within plan; no port, login policy, OAuth scopes or free JSON, and a secret-shaped name or value is refused. Under the same idempotency ledger as restart.

capabilities.title: Restart an application
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-535 (P-0035 Part B) on mcp-server's OAuth-protected /platform toolset: rolling restart of an application or one named service, under an idempotency key that deploy-api's durable ledger honours (same key + same request → same answer, no second side effect; changed request → conflict; keys never alias across actor, organization or client). Requires platform:apps:restart; platform:apps:write never substitutes.

capabilities.title: Delete an application
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-536 (P-0035 Part B) as exactly platform_app_delete_plan and platform_app_delete_execute. Plan is read-only and binds the owner/admin OAuth subject, organization, client, grant, exact scope, role, canonical app id/alias, live generation/revision, normalized permanent effects and digest to a random 192-bit request id with a 10-minute TTL. Only the same still-owner/admin human can approve or deny on the CSRF-protected console.<domain>/connector/approvals/<request_id> page; MCP exposes no decision or direct-delete tool. Execute accepts only request_id, revalidates every binding and the live revision under the app lock, atomically redeems server-side approval before one delete/audit row, and durably replays the same terminal result (or IN_PROGRESS) without a second side effect. The request id locates state but never authenticates its holder.

capabilities.title: List deployments
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-537 (P-0035 Part B) on mcp-server's OAuth-protected /platform toolset as the deployments family: platform_deployments_list (history from the app's Dibbla-managed main branch, one commit per deploy, plus live status), platform_deployment_get (one revision) and platform_deployment_logs (the current deployment's bounded log window; needs platform:logs:read as well). Read only: no start, no rollback. Listed in tools/list only for a grant holding the scope, and refused server-side otherwise.

capabilities.title: Create an agent-authored deployment proposal
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-537 (P-0035 Part B) on mcp-server's OAuth-protected /platform toolset as the deployment_proposals family: platform_deployment_proposal_create (a branch in the caller's push namespace, pinned at its head; title and description; an Idempotency-Key that replays to the same proposal; no environment variables, no secret values, no build options) and, under the same scope — the registry defines it as 'create and inspect' — platform_deployment_proposals_list, _get and _events. There is no approve, deny, apply, close or retry tool; the decision stays in the console (P-0034), and a test pins tools/list against one ever appearing.

capabilities.title: Start a deployment
capabilities.note: Scope and eventual state are fixed by P-0035 Part A so the contract can be reviewed before the tool exists. Part A exposes no /platform tool.

capabilities.title: Read a bounded application log window
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-534 (P-0035 Part B) on mcp-server's OAuth-protected /platform toolset; listed in tools/list only for a grant holding the scope, and refused server-side otherwise.

capabilities.title: List secret names and metadata
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-538 (P-0035 Part B) on mcp-server's OAuth-protected /platform toolset; listed in tools/list only for a grant holding the scope, and refused server-side otherwise. A secret value is never returned by any tool.

capabilities.title: Set or rotate a secret
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-538 (P-0035 Part B) on mcp-server's OAuth-protected /platform toolset; listed in tools/list only for a grant holding the scope, and refused server-side otherwise. A secret value is never returned by any tool. A set on an existing name rotates it; routine write with an idempotency key.

capabilities.title: Delete a secret
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-538 (P-0035 Part B) on mcp-server's OAuth-protected /platform toolset. Routine write with an idempotency key under the same write scope P-0035 assigns to set/rotate/delete; not remote-destructive, because there is no secrets destructive scope and the proposal's plan/confirm flow is for app, database and storage deletion.

capabilities.title: List managed databases
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-540 as platform_databases_list with cursor pagination. Returns only organization-owned name, PostgreSQL version, linked app, creation time, size, table count and phase; never DSN, host, user, password or secret material.

capabilities.title: Inspect bounded database metadata
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-540 as platform_database_get. Returns the same explicit metadata allowlist as list after organization ownership validation; no schema, row data or credentials.

capabilities.title: Read database lifecycle status
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-540 as platform_database_status. Returns provisioning, ready, restoring or failed with only the bounded database metadata allowlist.

capabilities.title: Run a bounded structured read-only SELECT
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-540 as platform_database_rows_query and intentionally absent from tools/list under metadata-only platform:databases:read. The caller supplies one database, one public base table, explicit catalog-validated columns, typed eq|in|lt|lte|gt|gte|is_null filters, at most one order_by, cursor and limit — never SQL, schema, join, view, CTE, function, expression, offset or wildcard. The server builds one parametrized SELECT with a SELECT-only role and read-only transaction, and enforces 100 rows, two seconds and 256 KiB. Audit stores actor and shape but never filter or cell values.

capabilities.title: Provision a managed database
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-540 as platform_database_provision(name, app_alias?, idempotency_key). Returns a durable database_provision operation immediately; identical normalized retries replay it and changed payloads conflict. Deploy-api persists, leases and resumes the work, while the generic operation tools expose status, events, logs, output and cancel.

capabilities.title: Restore a database from a backup
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-540 as platform_database_restore(name, source_file_id, idempotency_key). The opaque source_file_id binds a ready immutable hash- and size-bound file object in the same organization; transfer IDs, hashes, tickets, sessions and bytes are never restore identities. Restore is create-only and returns a durable database_restore operation immediately.

capabilities.title: Delete a managed database
capabilities.note: Scope and eventual state are fixed by P-0035 Part A so the contract can be reviewed before the tool exists. Part A exposes no /platform tool.

capabilities.title: List object-storage buckets
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-541 (P-0035 Part B / P-0026) as platform_storage_buckets_list and platform_storage_bucket_get. Both return only tenant-owned bucket name, quota, used bytes, object count, optional deployment, four secret names, creation time and status; credentials, endpoints, MinIO details, policies and object contents cannot enter the response. Platform and connector buckets are absent from this surface.

capabilities.title: Create a bucket with scoped credentials
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-541 (P-0035 Part B / P-0026) as synchronous platform_storage_bucket_provision. A required idempotency key binds the actor, organization, client, target and payload; exact retry replays, changed payload conflicts. The control plane creates the hard quota, lifecycle rule, bucket-scoped service account and four STORAGE_<NAME>_* secrets atomically from the caller's perspective, and never returns credential material.

capabilities.title: Rotate bucket credentials
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-541 (P-0035 Part B / P-0026) as synchronous, idempotent platform_storage_bucket_rotate under the narrow rotate scope. The old credential is invalidated, the two credential secrets are replaced and every service in a bound deployment must accept a restart before success; there is no no_restart input. Organization-global buckets report that restart is not applicable. Credential material is never returned.

capabilities.title: Delete a bucket
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-541 (P-0035 Part B / P-0026) as exactly platform_storage_bucket_delete_plan and platform_storage_bucket_delete_execute. The 10-minute random request binds owner/admin subject, organization, client, grant, role, exact scope, bucket identity, current credential-free metadata, normalized force-delete effects and digest. Only the same authenticated human approves in the CSRF-protected console; MCP has no decision, direct-delete or force tool. Execute accepts only request_id, revalidates metadata, atomically claims once, then force-deletes all objects, bucket, service account, ownership and four secrets while concurrent/retried calls receive IN_PROGRESS or the same terminal result. Platform and connector buckets never enter this surface.

capabilities.title: List workflows and revisions
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-539 (P-0035 Part B2) on mcp-server's /platform toolset as platform_workflows_list, platform_workflow_get, platform_workflow_revisions, platform_workflow_tools and platform_workflow_validate (validate saves nothing). Read through core's slim API under the verified principal; a workflow in another organization is NOT_FOUND.

capabilities.title: Create or update a workflow definition
capabilities.note: Scope and eventual state are fixed by P-0035 Part A so the contract can be reviewed before the tool exists. Part A exposes no /platform tool.

capabilities.title: Execute a workflow at a pinned immutable revision
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-539 (P-0035 Part B2/B3) as platform_workflow_execute: starts the run at HEAD asynchronously with a required idempotency_key (same key + same request replays the run, a different request under the same key is IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_CONFLICT) and returns the durable operation envelope wrapping the canonical run id. Pinning a named immutable revision is a later addition.

capabilities.title: Prepare a principal-bound browser download
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-543 (P-0035 Part B4) as platform_file_download_prepare plus platform_file_transfer_status. MCP accepts only opaque source_file_id and idempotency_key, creates a principal-bound transfer intent and returns safe metadata plus a Dibbla resource/fallback link. deploy-api mints the DIB-542 one-time ticket during prepare and stores only its AEAD-encrypted envelope. The same authenticated human opens console.<domain>/connector/transfers/<transfer_id>; the server redeems that ticket outside model context, replaces the envelope with an encrypted short-lived session, and gives only that browser the Dibbla-Transfer session for direct byte-plane access. No ticket, session, byte URL, presigned URL, file content or base64 enters MCP/model context, logs or audit. One opaque core UUID is the transfer_id reused unchanged by broker, deploy-api, MCP and UI; it locates state but never authorizes it. Crash recovery may atomically replace encrypted ticket/session material server-side for that same active transfer, but never creates a second ID, leaves two credentials valid or returns a credential to MCP/model context. Every actor/human read rechecks organization, user, client, grant and exact operation.

capabilities.title: Prepare a principal-bound resumable browser upload
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-543 (P-0035 Part B4) as platform_file_upload_prepare plus platform_file_transfer_abort; DIB-670 (Part F) adds an agent-redeemed second path over the same machinery. Direction-bound platform_file_transfer_status requires platform:files:write for the caller's own upload and platform:files:read for a download; download prepare always requires platform:files:read. Prepare accepts only name, content_type, exact content_length, content_sha256 and idempotency_key—never a byte/base64 field—and returns a principal-bound intent with safe metadata, the authenticated fallback link and, for a grant that can write, an upload plan naming this resource's own origin. Who redeems the one-time ticket is the only difference between the two paths. Browser-mediated: the authenticated human opens the console page, whose browser verifies every declared field, redeems the encrypted ticket outside model context and uploads chunks with Dibbla-Transfer. Agent-redeemed: the client process PUTs bounded chunks to <resource-origin>/platform/v1/file-transfers/<transfer_id>/bytes with Upload-Offset, authenticating with its own platform access token for the same grant; the first chunk redeems the ticket server-side. That URL carries no signature, ticket or session—it locates one transfer and the token decides—so a redeemed, expired or foreign-principal redemption is refused as absent, and it is a structured field the client acts on rather than prose the model repeats. Both paths share one transfer_id, one intent ledger, one resume offset and the uncached live-grant check that stops the next chunk after a revoke. Declared length or sha256 that does not hold ends the intent and produces no file. Completion publishes only the opaque source_file_id back to MCP. Abort is idempotent and never deletes a completed file. Ticket/session plaintext, presigned storage URLs and bytes are absent from the durable intent ledger, MCP results, model context, logs and audit.

capabilities.title: Delete a file
capabilities.note: Scope and eventual state are fixed by P-0035 Part A so the contract can be reviewed before the tool exists. Part A exposes no /platform tool.

capabilities.title: Poll a durable operation by its principal-bound ID
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-539 (P-0035 Part B3) as platform_operation_status, platform_operation_events, platform_operation_logs and platform_operation_output; extended by DIB-540 to database-operation IDs. Typed phase and cursor-paged content come from the resource's durable engine. The operation id is data, never authentication; an operation in another organization is NOT_FOUND.

capabilities.title: Cancel a durable operation
capabilities.note: Shipped by DIB-539 (P-0035 Part B3) as platform_operation_cancel and extended by DIB-540 to database-operation IDs: idempotent, valid only while cancellable, CONFLICT once finished; a terminal state is never rewritten.

capabilities.title: Switch the local CLI context
capabilities.reason: Local state, and a model-controlled context switch is forbidden outright: the connector URL selects the installation and the OAuth grant selects user and org.

capabilities.reason: Uses the OS keyring and a TTY.
